## Context

Competitive mode's win condition is first-to-threshold (parent CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30, phase-machine sibling). The producer explicitly asked for an endless continuation beyond threshold. - Endless-mode trigger and state handling after the win threshold is first reached (continue playing beyond threshold; scoring/phase semantics while beyond threshold).

- Competitive state model / phase machine / income routing / AI / harness / rendering — those are CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 and its children.
- Denial reasoning (separate follow-up).

- [ ] **AC1:** Endless mode wiring is defined via an explicit opt-in flag/config: what triggers continuation, what happens to win detection/score/endReason/gameResult when play continues beyond threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Deterministic behaviour — same seed + same actions produce the same endless-mode outcome.
- [ ] **AC3:** Competitive mode remains playable without engaging endless mode (players can stop at the threshold win; default behaviour unchanged).

# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** – Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card (1024×1024 source; eliminate generic Fallback art) (open)
- **MS-0MTIIL6J200291ZQ** – Per-owner income routing; shared event/incident resolution (open)
- **MS-0MUE2U21C0007BKL** – [test-failure] upgrade-drag-drop.browser.test.ts > animates the transfer from the drop location and plays the upgrade SFX (beginDrag timeout) — failing test (completed)

## Goal (user story)

As a player who just reached the win threshold in endless mode, I want an "Enter Endless Mode" button on the end-game dialog so I can continue playing beyond the threshold.

## Context

CG-0MTIILU5V006GCN4 wired the endless-mode logic: when `config.endlessMode === true` and a player reaches the score threshold, the engine sets `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and keeps `gameResult = 'playing'`. The end-game dialog (`MainStreetOverlayContent.showGameOverOverlay`) already reads `endReason` for display, but the player has no way to actually continue — the only options are "Play Again" (restart) and "Menu" (quit). This leaves the endless-mode feature inert from a player-facing perspective.

## Scope

- Add an "Enter Endless Mode" button to the end-game dialog when `endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- When pressed, the button dismisses the overlay and resumes gameplay from the current state (no restart).
- The button is hidden in all other end-reasons (normal win, bankruptcy, turn exhaustion, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Competitive mode endless mode (separate CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 children).
- UI changes to the main menu or difficulty selector.
- Any Monte Carlo or AI changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** End-game dialog shows an "Enter Endless Mode" button when `state.endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- [ ] **AC2:** Pressing the button dismisses the game-over overlay, resets `endReason` to `null` (or appropriate continuation value), and resumes the game loop — the game continues playing and scoring.
- [ ] **AC3:** The button is not shown when `endReason` is anything other than `score_threshold_continue`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showGameOverOverlay()` adds the button.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Resume logic after button press (dismiss overlay, call engine continuation).
- `tests/main-street/` — New or updated tests covering button appearance/dismiss/resume.

# Intake Brief: Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (MS-0MUNB54KU005084C)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from the "write storylines" epic (`MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV`), C6
> documentation roadmap. The epic commits a generated Mermaid flowchart at
> `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`; this item renders it to a portable
> image so the graph is viewable without a Mermaid-aware renderer and links it
> from the canonical storyline doc.

## Problem statement

The storyline graph is committed only as a Mermaid source file
(`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd`). Anyone reading the repository on a
plain Markdown viewer, on GitHub without Mermaid support, or in a rendered docs
artefact cannot see the graph and cannot easily tell the shape of the shipped
storylines. Rendering it to a portable SVG in a documented docs step and
linking it from `docs/main-street/storylines.md` makes the graph viewable
everywhere, without requiring a Mermaid-aware renderer.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — need to see the storyline shape at a
  glance in the docs, without installing Mermaid tooling.
  - *"As a content designer, I want the storyline graph shown as an image in the
    docs, so I can inspect the shipped chains without a Mermaid renderer."*
- **Developers / reviewers** — need the rendered graph to stay in sync with the
  committed Mermaid source so reviews trust the picture.
  - *"As a reviewer, I want a drift guard between the rendered image and the
    committed `.mmd`, so a stale graph cannot be merged."*
- **Docs build / maintainers** — need a deterministic, reproducible render step
  with no manual copy-paste.
  - *"As a maintainer, I want one documented command that regenerates the
    rendered graph, so the artefact is reproducible."*

## Acceptance Criteria

> **Finalised** per producer answers to Q1–Q3 (2026-10-07): minimal npm render
> step (A); reuse Playwright + `mermaid` devDependency (B); SVG-vs-`.mmd` drift
> guard (A).

1. **Rendered artefact** — a rendered graph image (`docs/main-street/storyline-graph.svg`)
   is committed under `docs/main-street/` and is viewable without a
   Mermaid-aware renderer (SVG preferred; PNG only if SVG cannot be emitted).
2. **Reproducible render step** — a documented npm script renders the committed
   `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` into the committed image
   deterministically (no RNG, timestamp or wall-clock input; byte-identical on
   re-run). The renderer is a **devDependency only** and does not enter the
   game bundle.
3. **Doc link** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` embeds or links the rendered
   image (in §7.2 "The shipped graph" and/or §11 "Related documents"),
   documenting the new regeneration command in the §5 tooling table.
4. **Drift guard (validation)** — an automated test/check fails when the
   committed rendered SVG drifts from the committed `.mmd`. The existing
   `.mmd`-vs-`src/card-data.csv` `--check` guard must continue to pass.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No mandatory new runtime dependency for the game** — any renderer
  dependency is a **devDependency** only and must not enter the game bundle.
  Reuse the already-installed `playwright` Chromium (no second Chromium
  download).
- **Determinism** — the render must be reproducible from the committed `.mmd`;
  no timestamps/ids embedded in the output that would churn on every run.
- **Mermaid is the source of truth** — the `.mmd` remains the generated
  artefact of record; the image is derived, never hand-edited.
- **Licensing** — any added dependency must be permissively licensed (MIT,
  Apache-2.0, CC0). The `mermaid` package is MIT.
- **Scope** — do not redesign the graph content or the storyline model, and do
  not build a full static docs site (deferred to `MS-0MUYK064P0032374`). This
  item only renders and links the existing graph.

## Existing state (repo research)

- `docs/main-street/storyline-graph.mmd` — committed 98-line Mermaid flowchart;

# Intake Brief: Level-2 Upgrade Prerequisite Gate Blocks Expensive-Tier Adoption

**Work item:** MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4 · `task` · `high`
**Discovered from:** MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M (Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance)
**Producer decisions:** Q1→(a), Q2→(a), Q3→(a) — see Appendix.

## Headline

On the canonical greedy Monte Carlo profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, Medium) four level-2 upgrades — `upg-grand-bakehouse`, `upg-restaurant`, `upg-multiplex`, `upg-luxury-retreat` — still sit at **0% M1 pick rate** and **0% M5 adoption**, because the AI almost never advances their parent businesses to level 1. This item re-tunes the *level-1 prerequisite cards'* `cost` values (card-data only) so the level-2 tier becomes reachable through the intended two-step chain, while leaving the level gate itself (US-19) intact.

## Problem statement

Level-2 upgrades are structurally gated: the AI emits a `buy-upgrade` action only when a business satisfies `biz.name === card.targetBusiness && biz.level === requiredLevel && biz.level < biz.maxLevel` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`). The four level-2 upgrades carry `requiredLevel: 1`, so they need a parent already at level 1. The greedy AI advances only ~7–13% of parents to level 1, so the intersection of *(level-2 card in market) × (parent at level 1) × (affordable)* is effectively zero. Cost/`incomeBonus` changes on the level-2 cards themselves cannot move adoption (Experiment B preserved 0% M1), because the binding constraint is upstream: too few level-1 parents exist.

## Users

- **Player** — wants the late-game investment tier to be a real choice (e.g. "My Diner is doing well — should I push it to a full Restaurant?"). Today the most powerful upgrades in the pool are unreachable in practice.
- **Producer / designer** — wants the level-2 chain to function as designed (a two-step progression reward) and to be demonstrably reachable in the canonical simulation, without weakening the chain design.
- **Developer** — wants a small, reversible card-data change with before/after Monte Carlo evidence, consistent with the parent item's card-data-only precedent.

User story: *As a player running a profitable Bakery, I want a path to the Grand Bakehouse to be realistically attainable, so that investing in a favourite business pays off over a full run.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline and before/after evidence captured.** On the canonical profile (200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, `greedy`, sweep Easy/Medium/Hard — command below), record M1 pick rate for the four level-2 upgrades and M5 adoption for the four parents (Bakery, Diner, Cinema, Day Spa) and their level-1 prerequisites, both before and after the change, commit-stamped in the work-item description.
2. **Target reachable.** All four level-2 upgrades reach **≥5% M1** on the canonical Medium profile, with a non-zero absolute purchase count.
3. **Leading indicator rises.** Level-1 parent adoption (M5 for `upg-patisserie`/`upg-bread-factory`, `upg-bistro`/`upg-fast-food`, `upg-imax`/`upg-drive-in`, `upg-resort-spa`/`upg-wellness-center`) measurably increases versus the captured baseline.
4. **Gate and chain preserved.** The four level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`, and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` still enforces level equality (PRD-milestone-2 US-19 AC2/AC3 unchanged). No engine-rule changes in this item.
5. **Ladder preserved.** Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard win-rate ordering is retained and the Medium win-rate moves within ±0.05 of the pre-change baseline.
6. **Testing and validation.** A Vitest test asserts the canonical card-data invariant (the four level-2 upgrades have `requiredLevel: 1`) and the M1/M5 metric computation used for the before/after evidence; the full project test suite passes with the new values.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` and `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` are updated where the re-derived costs are referenced; code comments touched by the change are updated.

## Constraints

- **Card-data values only** (`src/card-data.csv`, and only `cost` / `incomeBonus` fields). No engine-rule, AI-priority, or deck-mechanic changes in this item.
- **Preserve US-19** (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md`): level-2 upgrades keep `requiredLevel: 1`; `canPurchaseUpgrade()` equality is unchanged; the two-step chain described in `card-catalog.md` remains valid.
- **If the ≥5% target is unreachable** within card-data-only tuning, raise a **separate** engine/deck work item (e.g. a per-card market weight/copies column or a shared upgrade-deck `copies` change) rather than expanding this item's scope.
- Adjustments must be minimal and reversible, with commit-stamped before/after evidence.
- Win-rate ladder Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard must be preserved.
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

Canonical profile: 200 seeds, prefix `mc-balance`, 60 max turns, greedy, Medium (current `dev` tip). Six upgrades at **0% M1 / 0% M5**:

| Upgrade | Level req. | Parent | Card `cost` | Outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| `upg-museum` | 0 | Art Gallery (rare) | 700 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-dental-clinic` | 0 | Dentist (rare) | 700 | 0% (7.1% when cost→300) |
| `upg-grand-bakehouse` | 1 | Bakery | 900 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-restaurant` | 1 | Diner | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-multiplex` | 1 | Cinema | 1400 | 0% M1 |
| `upg-luxury-retreat` | 1 | Day Spa | 1400 | 0% M1 |

Parent purchase counts across 200 runs: Bakery 44, Diner 38, Cinema 34, Day Spa 7. Level-1 parents (of 200): Bakery ~4, Diner ~8, Cinema ~4, Day Spa ~4.

Prior experiments (recorded on the work item): removing the gate lifts the four level-2 upgrades to 2.9–10.3% M1 (isolates the gate); aggressive level-2 cost/bonus cuts leave them at 0% M1; boosting level-1 prerequisite `incomeBonus` barely moves level-1 adoption because the AI's Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unconditional; lowering `upg-dental-clinic` cost 700→300 alone reached 7.1% M1. **Cost (affordability) is the only score-independent card-data lever not yet fully tested.**

Reproduce the baseline:

```bash
npx vite-node src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts \
  --sweep --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 60 \
  --sweep-strategies greedy --sweep-difficulties Easy,Medium,Hard \
  --out results/level2-gate-before.json
```

M1/M5 are derived from `MonteCarloRunSummary.marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` via the balance-analysis API (`computePickRate`, `computeUpgradeAdoption`; see `docs/main-street/balance-analysis-api.md`).

## Desired change

Re-tune the **level-1 prerequisite cards'** `cost` values down (and their `incomeBonus` only where cost alone is insufficient) so that materially more parents reach level 1, and, if required, reduce the level-2 cards' `cost` so an existing level-1 parent can afford the second step. The gate stays in place; the chain is preserved. Concretely, candidates are the expensive level-1 branches — `upg-bread-factory` (700), `upg-fast-food` (700), `upg-imax` (700), `upg-drive-in` (700), `upg-wellness-center` (900), `upg-resort-spa` (900) — plus the level-2 `cost`s (`upg-grand-bakehouse` 900; `upg-restaurant`/`upg-multiplex`/`upg-luxury-retreat` 1400). Evidence must show which lever did the work.

If card-data tuning proves insufficient to reach ≥5% M1, document the shortfall and create the follow-up engine/deck work item; do not change engine rules here.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — adjust `cost` (and `incomeBonus` where justified) for the six level-1 prerequisite cards and, if needed, the four level-2 cards; do **not** change `requiredLevel`.
- `src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts` — canonical profile runner (sweep mode, `mc-balance` seeds, 60 turns).
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — run loop; source of `marketOffers` / `cardsOwned` per-card metrics.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `buy-upgrade` action generation (level-gate matching) and Priority-2/3 selection; read-only reference for the gate semantics.
- `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — `canPurchaseUpgrade()` and the level/`displayName` mutation on upgrade application.
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — US-19 (Multi-Level Upgrade Chains) constraint; read-only.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — multi-level upgrade chain description and cost references.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — upgrade cost formula used to re-derive values.
- `core/src/balance-cards/` — balance cost-curve helpers (used by `run-balance-cards`), if re-derivation uses them.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` — existing balance-card tests; extend for the invariant test.
- `src/scripts/balance/baseline-blocks.ts` — baseline/target blocks used by guardrail checks.

## Related work

- MS-0MUR9I9WO004EW0M — Re-evaluate upgrade costs/ROI after the 5-turn payback rebalance (source item; `blocked`, card-data-only precedent).
- MS-0MUQ50I1Y000B6L3 — Game balance: business payback to ~5 turns and economy re-tune (completed; introduced the payback regime).
- MS-0MUQUBK1B006EODZ — After-state Monte Carlo, guardrails and baseline (completed; canonical profile definition).
- MS-0MUQUBJQF009PTZ0 — Re-tune compensating balance levers (completed).
- MS-0MUVPB1UE004UUBI / MS-0MUUYI950004TG7F — upgrade ownership/regression tests (completed; test precedent).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** – Playable AI competitive mode (human vs AI) (completed)
- **MS-0MUML5X1L008LT8Z** – Implement Physiotherapist rename across all files (completed)
- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** – Render the storyline graph (Mermaid to SVG) in the docs build (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, action, affordable, alone, already (+134 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, action, alone, already, bakehouse (+117 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: action, adoption, affordable, alone, already (+115 more)

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MUXAL8HC005P9E4.md`.

## Assumptions

- The M1/M5 formulas and canonical profile remain stable; comparisons are like-for-like at the same seed/strategy/difficulty.
- The greedy AI's unconditional Priority-3 upgrade purchase is unchanged (no AI edits in scope), so affordability and market co-occurrence are the operative levers.
- `200 seeds` gives adequate resolution for a ≥5% target (5% ≈ 1.5 purchases of ~30 appearances; small-n noise is acknowledged and the leading indicator plus absolute counts are reported alongside).

## Risks

- **Small-n noise**: M1 on ~30 appearances is coarse; a ≥5% target could pass/fail by chance. *Mitigation:* report absolute purchase counts and the level-1 leading indicator; consider a larger seed count for the decisive run.
- **Card-data tuning insufficient**: if level-1 adoption cannot be lifted enough without an engine/deck change, the ≥5% target may be unreachable in scope. *Mitigation:* explicit escalation path to a separate engine work item (documented, not silent scope creep).
- **Ladder regression**: cheaper upgrades may shift win rates. *Mitigation:* AC4 ladder check with the ±0.05 Medium band.
- **Scope creep**: other zero-adoption cards (`upg-museum`, `upg-dental-clinic` with rare parents) invite broadening. *Mitigation:* keep them out of scope; log as separate work if needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix direction, given US-19).** Which approach should this item implement? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Preserve US-19 and the two-step chain; lift level-2 reachability by re-tuning level-1 prerequisite costs (card-data-only, matching the parent's "cost + incomeBonus only" scope); escalate to an engine/deck change as a separate work item only if the ≥5% target is unreachable. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (acceptance criteria).** Keep the proposed targets *plus* a level-1 leading-indicator AC? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Yes — keep the proposed ACs and add the level-1 leading indicator. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (scope boundary).** Card-data values only, or allow a minimal engine/deck change in this item? — **Answer (operator): (a)** Card-data values only first; spin off any engine change as a new work item. Source: interactive reply.

Research note (agent): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` US-19 AC2/AC3 require `requiredLevel: 1` and `canPurchaseUpgrade()` level equality; the original "Experiment A" (`requiredLevel 1→0`) would break a committed PRD AC and the chain, so option (a) was adopted. Experiment C's null result is explained by the AI's unconditional Priority-3 purchase, which makes `incomeBonus` score-independent and leaves `cost` (affordability) as the viable card-data lever.

# Perform end of turn phase for each player (MS-0MUXAQQON006XA6I)

## Problem statement

In competitive (human vs AI) mode the shared closing (Income → Incident → EndCheck) is presented as a single condensed, text-only summary. The full end-of-turn income choreography that single-player players see — base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD coin collection, with per-card coin grids and sound — never runs for the AI seats (nor for the human seat). Much of the end-of-turn phase is therefore lost in an AI game.

## Users

- **Competitive mode players** (especially the human seat) who want to see the outcome of each player's day — what each seat earned and what effects fired — with the same visual feedback as single-player, rather than an unexplained jump to the next day.
- **Maintainers** who want a single end-of-turn presentation path so the single-player and competitive flows cannot drift.

Example user stories:
- "As a competitive player, after I end my day I want to watch each player's income collection in turn, so I understand how the shared day changed every seat's economy."
- "As a competitive player on a slow machine, I want the AI closing to be short and skippable, so playing against AI does not take many minutes per day."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1: Per-seat full closing presentation** — After the shared competitive closing resolves, the presentation runs the full phased income choreography (`animateIncomePhases`: base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD collection) once per non-eliminated seat, in seat order, using that seat's own income/effects. The human seat is included; eliminated seats are skipped.
- **AC2: Authoritative per-seat data** — The competitive closing surfaces the per-owner income (`applyCompetitiveIncome` → `OwnerIncomeResult[]`, which already carries a full `IncomeResult.phaseBreakdown`) instead of discarding it, and every presented per-seat value equals the delta actually applied to that `PlayerRecord` (asserted by test).
- **AC3: Per-seat income feedback text** — The closing summary reports each seat's income (e.g. `Player 2: +7 coins`), not the shared host total, which can differ from any player's actual income.
- **AC4: Shared engine semantics unchanged** — Presentation-only change: the closing order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), the single shared incident per day, and seeded-replay determinism are unchanged.
- **AC5: Single presentation primitive** — Single-player and competitive closings are driven by one shared presentation path; `finishTurnPresentation` and `presentCompetitiveClosing` no longer duplicate the income/incident/end-of-turn/advance logic. Single-player behaviour is behaviourally unchanged (existing turn-flow tests pass without modification). This absorbs **MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ**.
- **AC6: Bounded and non-blocking** — Full animations run in normal play; reduced motion, replay and headless contexts fall back to per-seat text and always advance the day; a global fast-forward bound caps total closing time so a large roster cannot stall the game (honours MS-0MUVUPRXZ0030LUD AC4).
- **AC7: Tests** — New/updated automated tests cover: per-seat animation sequencing (one full choreography per non-eliminated seat, in order), authoritative per-seat values (presented == applied deltas), bounded/headless fallback (day always advances; text-only when animations are disabled), and single-player unchanged.
- **AC8: Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Presentation-only** (producer decision Q2-A): no change to the engine closing order or the shared-incident contract; income/incident still resolve once per shared day.
- **Bounded** (producer decision Q3-A): the closing must never block the day start indefinitely; reduced motion / replay / headless degrade to text.
- **Determinism**: the presentation must not consume RNG or mutate state (beyond reusing the existing deferred-delta window where applicable), so seeded replay stays reproducible.
- **Single-player parity**: single-player end-of-turn presentation and its deferred-mutation flow (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q) must not regress.
- Phaser-free helpers where possible, so the node integration tests can exercise the flow (`MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive` is already Phaser-free).

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
  - `endCompetitiveTurnDay` → `driveAiSeatsUntilClosing` → `runCompetitiveClosing` → `presentCompetitiveClosing` → `startTurnPhase`.
  - `presentCompetitiveClosing` shows `Resolving end-of-turn effects...`, a one-line `competitiveClosingSummary` built from the **shared** `result.income.total` and the incident name, then `End of turn complete.` after a ~900 ms hold. It deliberately does **not** run `animateIncomePhases` (test `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts` asserts `incomeCalls` is empty).
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` calls `applyCompetitiveIncome(state)` and **discards** the returned `OwnerIncomeResult[]`; `TurnResult.income` carries only the shared `applyIncome` result. `applyCompetitiveIncome` already builds a per-owner `IncomeResult` with a full `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — single-player `endTurn` delegates to `processEndOfTurn` (with `deferResourceApplication`) then `animateIncomePhases`, then `finishTurnPresentation`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateIncomePhases(animator, phaseData, options)` runs the phased choreography from `SlotPhaseBreakdown[]` (indexed against the shared street grid) and applies `options.pendingDeltas` exactly once at collection completion; `incomeCollectionActive` gates the HUD delta pop.

### AC1 — before/after evidence (greedy, 200 seeds, mc-balance, 60 turns)

Recipe: `npx vite-node src/scripts/monte-carlo.ts --sweep --seeds 200 --seed-prefix mc-balance --maxTurns 60 --sweep-strategies greedy --sweep-difficulties Easy,Medium,Hard --out results/level2-gate-{before,after}.json`. | Easy | 0.800 → 0.795 | ✔ |

### AC2 — target reachable: **UNMET**

M1 pick rate (purchases / market appearances), before → after:

| Capstone | Easy | Medium | Hard |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upg-grand-bakehouse` | 3.7% (1/27) → 3.7% (1/27) | 2.8% (1/36) → 2.8% (1/36) | 2.7% (1/37) → 2.7% (1/37) |

Level-1 prerequisite M1 (Medium): `upg-bread-factory` 14.3%→14.3%, `upg-fast-food` 3.8%→3.7%, `upg-drive-in` **2.9%→8.3%**, `upg-wellness-center` 0%→0%. Hard: bread-factory 7.4%→11.1%, fast-food 3.2%→6.7%, drive-in 4.0%→8.0%, wellness 7.7%→4.0%.

Easy ≥ Medium ≥ Hard preserved; Medium win-rate moved −0.005 (within ±0.05).

See file list above.

### Root-cause finding (why AC2 is unreachable in scope)

Cost is **not** the binding constraint. An even more aggressive variant (level-1 cost 200, level-2 cost 400) produced **identical** adoption, because affordability never binds — the AI usually has enough coins. The capstone only converts when a level-1 parent and the capstone card **co-occur in a run**, and the market shows at most **one upgrade per turn** drawn from a 78-card upgrade deck (39 templates × 2 copies).
